title: Capacity event: noisy-neighbor spike RCA and synthetic safeguard playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the 2026-02-28 capacity incident a single tenant produced sustained microbursts that exhausted KV cache slots and starved co-located tenants, causing elevated tail latency and multiple eviction cascades. The event combined three contributing factors: (1) a tenant workload shift (short, high-frequency sequences) that made their effective token demand much higher than historical billing-derived reservations, (2) an overly permissive burst token grant that did not decay fast enough during continued high utilization, and (3) a blind spot in autoscaler heuristics that ignored sequence-length distributions when proposing reservation growth.

Goal:
Document RCA, define a small-surface, testable automated safeguard (synthetic request sentinel + preemptive reservation rebalance), and land conservative runtime and console controls to prevent recurrence while we build longer-term reservation autotuning and tenant fingerprinting features.
action_items: 1) Telemetry and evidence: add per-tenant sequence-length histogram to existing capacity dashboards; create an incident dashboard slice with KV cache eviction rate, burst token usage, and per-tenant slot utilization (owner: infra-observability, estimate: 2)

2) Synthetic sentinel: implement a lightweight synthetic request generator that imitates short-high-frequency patterns; run in each dedicated cluster as a health probe and raise alert if sentinel triggers > 95th percentile of KV eviction rate (owner: serving-runtime, estimate: 3)

3) Reservation safety net: implement preemptive small-scale reservation rebalance that grants temporary fractional reservation credits to affected tenants based on sentinel signal for up to 30m, with automated rollback (owner: allocator, estimate: 5)

4) Burst policy tightening: change burst decay from 10m linear to 3m exponential for tenants with sudden changes in sequence-length distribution, and add a per-tenant burst cap override for safety (owner: qos, estimate: 2)

5) Autoscaler improvement spike: add sequence-length-aware estimator in the autoscaler and run offline validation with historical traces to ensure proposals reduce under-reservation (owner: autoscale, estimate: 8)

6) Runbook and console: author a post-incident runbook that describes sentinel signals, manual mitigation steps, and console quick-actions to pin a tenant to a lower burst-class (owner: ops-docs, estimate: 1)

7) Canary + rollout: gate changes behind feature flag; deploy sentinel and burst-cap to 10% of clusters first, monitor for false positives and customer impact before wider rollout (owner: serving-runtime + SRE, estimate: 3)
8) Post-change verification: synthetic workload replay for top-10 customers on a staging cluster to verify no regressions in expected throughput/latency (owner: qa, estimate: 4)
9) Customer communication: prepare status note for impacted customers and include guidance on workload patterns that trigger spikes; coordinate with CSM for outreach (owner: support, estimate: 1)
10) Longer-term: design and schedule reservation-autotuner (adaptive reservations based on fingerprinting + smoothing policy) for Q2 roadmap (owner: research/infra, estimate: 13)

Acceptance criteria: each safety change must be behind FF, have a monitoring dashboard, alert runbook, and a rollback plan. Sentinel and burst-cap must produce <1% false-positive rate in 48h canary before 100% rollout.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage concluded; staff call on 2026-03-01 09:15. Collected GC/KV eviction traces and per-tenant request logs. Preliminary hypothesis: reservation mismatch + permissive burst policy.

2026-03-02 - Diego Morales: Confirmed tenant X had a 3x increase in median sequence length and 6x increase in short-window RPS. KV eviction rate spiked concurrently. Created trace links: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/incident/ENG-389207-kv-evictions
2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (SRE): Proposed sentinel approach in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INF/Sentinel+Synthetic+Probe+Design. Schedule design review 2026-03-04.

2026-03-05 - Design review notes: narrow sentinel to imitate 80% short sequences and 20% medium; ensure sentinel traffic excluded from billing and autoscaler inputs. Action: add an opt-out label for tenants that cannot accept synthetic probes.
2026-03-06 - Infra-observability: Dashboard PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/grafana-dashboards/pull/842. Added per-tenant sequence-length histograms and eviction-rate heatmap.
2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: PoC for burst-decay change landed in staging branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4231. Running 48h canary starting 2026-03-09.
2026-03-09 - QA: Synthetic replay started for top-10 customers. Early results show no throughput regressions; observe reduced eviction tail for synthetic sentinels in staging clusters.
2026-03-10 - PM (Lena Zhou): Approved communication draft for customers. Next steps: roll sentinel + burst-cap to 10% clusters and collect 72h telemetry before proceeding with autoscaler work.
Open follow-ups: Autoscaler estimator prototype (ENG-39512 referenced), reservation autotuner exploration ticket to be created and prioritized into Cycle 2026-W14.
